devops.title: DevOps & infrastructure
devops.lead: I run my own production server: 11 sites, automations and AI agents behind a single proxy. At NTT DATA, Kubernetes on AWS.
devops.diagramTitle: Infrastructure of my own server and the clouds I operate
devops.diagramDesc: Visitors and Telegram webhooks reach Caddy through DNS, and Caddy routes traffic into a Docker network with no public ports: on-demand WordPress with a shared MariaDB, the appsMonitor panel, n8n and the AI agent runner. Outside the VPS: Vercel, AWS and Cloudflare.

items.text: VPS on DigitalOcean
Provisioning script: Docker from the official repo, ufw, fail2ban, 2 GB swap and unattended-upgrades
Non-root user and key-only SSH
Reverse proxy with automatic TLS and a wildcard
DNS with a wildcard A record
n8n behind the proxy; the Telegram webhook only accepts Telegram's IP ranges
Docker Compose with a shared MariaDB and WordPress services enabled by profiles
Memory limit per site
Tools container
Caddy + n8n + AI agent runner stack with no public ports, header auth

panel.title: My own control panel (appsMonitor)

items.text: Fastify + TypeScript: starts and stops demos by reading Compose labels, with RAM, disk, load, uptime and a logs modal
Cap on demos running at once
Before starting a site it requires free memory and low load: a rule learned from a 12-minute outage
It used to be a systemd user service; today it's a container with the Docker socket mounted

mediaAlt: Droplet card in appsMonitor: 820 MB of 1.9 GB RAM free, disk at 37% with 29.6 GB free, 1-minute load of 0.09, 1 vCPU and 21 days of uptime
appsMonitor panel: project list with status and start/stop controls

items.text: Database and uploads
Restore with URL search-replace
Backup of the n8n workflows
Script that checks the live URLs respond
Weekly cron that sends the status to Telegram through n8n

automation.title: Automation with n8n and AI agents

items.text: n8n flows in production: sign-up, waitlist, public booking, booking bot, reminders and weekly status
In the AI agent pipeline: human approval with Wait + webhook, state in Postgres and rate limiting
Express service that runs Claude Code headless in Docker, with an idle watchdog and Chromium for screenshots
Context sync by script and model fallback when it runs out of memory (OOM)

mediaAlt: The six portfolio n8n flows grouped into capture, operations and management, with two Telegram bots split by channel
mediaCaption: The six portfolio flows. The two bots in the image are the portfolio's (alerts and bookings); the third one serves the AI agent pipeline.

items.text: Vercel: Neon from the Marketplace, env vars marked Sensitive and crons
AWS at NTT DATA: EKS, RDS Oracle, EC2 via SSM, Transit Gateway, S3, CloudWatch, Helm, KEDA, Karpenter, Istio and Terraform
AWS for 3Destiny: EC2 with SSM access and Route53
Cloudflare: tunnels to expose local demos
Playwright scripts: page sweeps, 404s and states
Layout clipping detector across the full width range

visitors.label: Visitors
visitors.detail: Any visit to a site or a demo. It comes in over HTTPS and resolves through DNS to the server's single proxy.

telegram.label: Telegram
telegram.detail: The Telegram bots call in by webhook. The proxy only accepts those requests when they come from Telegram's IP ranges.

dns.label: DNS
dns.detail: A wildcard A record points all of *.taller.works at the VPS. Adding a site doesn't touch DNS.

github.label: GitHub Actions
github.detail: The appsMonitor panel deploys from GitHub Actions: SSH, rsync and a service restart.

host.label: Host hardening
host.detail: What the provisioning script leaves on the host before a single container runs.

caddy.label: Caddy
caddy.detail: The server's single reverse proxy. It issues and renews certificates on its own, routes each subdomain to its container and is the only door into the internal network.

cron.label: Weekly cron
cron.detail: Every Monday at 9:00 the live URLs are checked for a 200 and the status reaches Telegram through n8n.

wordpress.label: WordPress × profiles
wordpress.detail: Each site is a Compose service enabled by profile: it starts when someone asks for it. Two fit at a time.

mariadb.label: MariaDB
mariadb.detail: A single database shared by every WordPress site: less memory than one per site.

appsmonitor.label: appsMonitor
appsmonitor.detail: My control panel: it starts and stops demos by reading Compose labels. Before starting one it checks memory and load, a rule that came from a 12-minute outage.

wpcli.label: wp-cli
wpcli.detail: Tools container for migrations, exports and search-replace without installing anything on the host.

backups.label: Backups
backups.detail: Database export and an uploads tarball per site; restore rewrites URLs with search-replace.

n8n.label: n8n · 6 flows
n8n.detail: Six flows in production: sign-ups, bookings, bots, reminders and the weekly status. Human approval with Wait + webhook and rate limiting.

runner.label: AI agent runner
runner.detail: Express service that runs Claude Code headless inside Docker. Only n8n calls it, from the internal network, with header auth.

vercel.label: Vercel · 13 projects
vercel.detail: The Next.js products live on Vercel, with Neon from the Marketplace, crons and variables marked Sensitive.

aws.label: AWS
aws.detail: At NTT DATA I work on Kubernetes on AWS; for 3Destiny, the client's EC2 with SSM access and DNS on Route53.

cloudflare.label: Cloudflare
cloudflare.detail: Cloudflare tunnels to show a demo running on my machine without opening ports.
